metadata.title: Secure Collaboration

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for enabling trusted, accountable, and appropriately bounded digital collaboration across institutional and external participants.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Collaboration platforms, messaging systems, conferencing services, persistent workspaces, and collaborative content environments.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Composite Secure Collaboration architecture composed of baseline collaboration trust, messaging, conferencing, presence signaling, content sharing, and persistent workspaces.

props.name: data-entity
props.remarks: Collaboration conversations, workspace state, presence indicators, shared artifacts, recordings, automation bindings, and collaboration audit metadata.

props.name: dependency-class
props.remarks: Secure Collaboration services are Tier-1 institutional dependencies supporting instruction, research, and operations.

props.name: depends-on-pattern
props.remarks: Secure Collaboration inherits baseline collaboration trust properties from Collaboration Core.

props.name: depends-on-pattern
props.remarks: Secure Collaboration relies on Secure Identity for authentication, attribution, role context, and delegation.

props.name: depends-on-pattern
props.remarks: Secure Collaboration relies on Secure Network for trusted transport, segmentation, monitoring, and resiliency.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Valid accounts are a primary attack vector against collaboration environments, enabling misuse, impersonation, and unauthorized persistence.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Masquerading and misleading identity representation undermine trust in collaboration contexts.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Collaboration inherently relies on trusted relationships, which may be abused through external or over-scoped participation.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Collaboration services may be abused as legitimate platforms for covert communication or data exfiltration.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Strong identity binding and attribution are essential to maintaining trust across collaboration modalities.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit boundary and membership enforcement mitigate unauthorized or unintended collaboration access.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Observability and auditability support accountability and detection of collaboration misuse.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Lifecycle governance reduces residual risk from abandoned or unmanaged collaboration spaces and artifacts.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Secure Collaboration services involving real-time voice and video align with NIST SP 800-58 guidance for securing VoIP and multimedia communication.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Collaboration commonly involves remote and unmanaged endpoints, requiring controls consistent with NIST SP 800-46.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Federated and cross-organizational collaboration scenarios align with NIST SP 800-47 trust-boundary guidance.

metadata.remarks: Secure Collaboration is the composite governance pattern defining why digital collaboration is treated as a distinct security domain. The ATT&CK and D3FEND references in this pattern serve as systemic rationale for institutional controls and do not represent implementation-level threat mitigation. Detailed threat handling and control mappings are defined in Collaboration Core and modality-specific patterns.
